blocks.text: A CA certificate is required for enrolling Zscaler Client Connector, enrolling AppProtection-enabled application segments, and when configuring an App Connector, configuring a Private Service Edge, configuring Network Connectors, and configuring a Private Cloud Controller for enrollment. Enrollment certificates differ from web server certificates. Web server certificates provide access to web applications. To learn more, see About Enrollment Certificates.

Zscaler recommends creating a certificate for Zscaler Client Connector, another certificate for App Connectors, a third for Private Service Edges, a fourth for Network Connectors, and a fifth for Private Cloud Controllers. If you have AppProtection enabled, you need to create an additional certificate.
To generate a Zscaler-issued enrollment certificate:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Enrollment Certificates.
Name: Enter a name for the certificate. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Type: Select one of the following options:
Root CA: Select to use a root certificate authority.
Intermediate CA: Select to use an intermediate certificate authority, then select a parent certificate, which can be a preloaded certificate or another Zscaler-issued certificate.
Client Certificate Type: Select one of the following options:
None: Select to use this enrollment certificate to enroll App Connectors, Private Service Edges, or Private Cloud Controllers.
Client Connector: Select to use this enrollment certificate to enroll Zscaler Client Connector.
Isolation Client: Select to use this enrollment certificate to enroll Zero Trust Browser clients.

Auto AppProtection CA: Select to use this enrollment certificate to enroll AppProtection-enabled application segments. If there is an existing certificate, and you create a new AppProtection CA certificate, it replaces the previous AppProtection CA certificate.
Store in HSM: Select True to store both the public and private keys for the generated certificate in a hardware security module (HSM) for additional protection.
